acceptance: Every Tier 3 benchmark exceeding its Phase 0 ADR budget has either (a) a merged vectorized Python implementation behind opt-in --datagen-backend native passing Gate A, Gate C (owner-approved acceptance report comparing legacy vs new distributions and all query row counts across DuckDB and DataFusion + frozen golden per-table hashes), and Gate D budget, OR (b) a recorded Gate D budget-miss report routing that benchmark to datagen-p2-rust-repo-gate.
Tier 3 benchmarks already within their Phase 0 ADR budget are explicitly recorded as no-action-needed.
Per-benchmark versioning is used in datagen_version.py with zero change to global DATA_GENERATION_VERSION; tsbs_devops uses an explicit default seed across all 5 tables (tags, cpu, mem, disk, net).
Each qualifying benchmark lands in its own PR (split into per-benchmark child TODOs if more than two benchmarks exceed budget), leaving legacy intact behind --datagen-backend legacy.
context: Phase 2 step 1 of the faster data-generation plan. Applies adr-python-core-runtime.md's first remedy (vectorized PyArrow/NumPy or embedded DuckDB SQL) to over-budget Tier 3 synthetic benchmarks before any Rust repository may be proposed.
description:
## Problem
Scalar Python loops and full-in-memory materialization make several non-TPC synthetic generators slow or memory-heavy at SF 1 and SF 10. Per docs/internal/adr/adr-python-core-runtime.md and owner decision A1, over-budget synthetic generators must be vectorized in Python first before considering a Rust repository.

## Change
- Using the empirical baselines and budgets from datagen-p0-baseline-measurements and datagen-p0-companion-adr, rank all Tier 3 candidates that exceed budget: h2odb, tsbs_devops (5 tables: tags, cpu, mem, disk, net), vector_search, coffeeshop, amplab, clickbench (synthetic mode), plus lower-priority joinorder_synthetic (repo_only) and tpch_skew (experimental).
- If more than two benchmarks exceed budget, create one child TODO and one PR per qualifying benchmark rather than shipping a monolithic PR.
- For each over-budget benchmark, implement a vectorized Python (NumPy/PyArrow; DuckDB is not a core dependency, so embedded DuckDB SQL is allowed only as an optional extra with a NumPy/PyArrow path for core installs) generator behind opt-in --datagen-backend native with explicit deterministic seeding (fixing tsbs_devops unseeded default_rng(None)) and bounded streaming I/O.
- Register a per-benchmark generator version in datagen_version.py (never bumping global DATA_GENERATION_VERSION).
- Execute Gate C validation per benchmark: exact row counts, zero orphan FKs, documented hit rates, a one-time owner acceptance report comparing legacy vs new distributions and every benchmark query's row count across DuckDB and DataFusion, and frozen golden per-table hashes + expected row counts.
- Measure wall time (mono_time()) and peak RSS under make heavy-run against the ADR's per-benchmark budget (Gate D).

## Decision gates
- Per benchmark: owner must approve the Gate C acceptance report before merging.
- Per benchmark: if vectorized Python meets the ADR budget -> eligible for datagen-p3-synthetic-cutover; ONLY if it still misses its ADR wall-time or peak-RSS budget after vectorization -> document the residual bottleneck and route to datagen-p2-rust-repo-gate.

## Guardrails
- Never use arbitrary 2–5% tolerance bands on deterministic output; freeze exact golden hashes after owner acceptance.
- Never bump global DATA_GENERATION_VERSION; keep legacy generators intact behind --datagen-backend legacy.
- Enforce [RUN-DATA-001] (isolated cache/provenance per backend version), [HEAVY-LOCK-001], [COMMENT-POLICY-001], and AGENTS.md PR closeout.
